A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PVI research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original Gaussian and regression simulations, golf and election analyses, cryoEM inference, and seven posteriordb benchmark evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds NUTS benchmark results, earnings-model diagnostics and timing, and a dimensional-scaling experiment.

M1.justification: v4 locally corrects the documented gradient computations: the quadratic estimator gains a missing derivative, and the CRPS estimator uses a difference rather than a sum inside the sign function (Table 1; A.4/A.6). The objectives, scoring rules, regularizers and variational families remain; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes or reruns.

E1.justification: The golf, election, cryoEM, Gaussian/regression and seven posteriordb tasks are retained. The added earnings diagnostics and Gaussian dimensional-scaling study extend analyses and configurations within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds HMC/NUTS as a reported comparator across all seven posteriordb models (Table 4), substantially extending a benchmark comparison previously limited to VI. NUTS already appeared as a sampler within v3's SBI procedures, but lacked this benchmark participation.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce default NumPyro NUTS settings and a Gaussian dimension sweep up to 10,000 using n=100, M=10 and a mean-field family (B.7). Existing benchmark splits and training budgets are retained. The scaling experiment's printed likelihood omits theta, leaving its precise model specification unclear.

E4.justification: New Sections B.6–B.7 examine earnings-model convergence, scoring-rule-dependent posterior shapes and computational costs, followed by sensitivity to parameter dimension. These materially expand the supplementary analyses to optimization behavior and scalability beyond the retained calibration, contamination and misspecification studies.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains means and standard deviations from five random seeds, and Figure 2 retains 50 simulations. The new NUTS table extends the same five-seed reporting practice; no increased run counts or new statistical estimation procedures are stated.

E6.justification: All original Table 2 numerical entries and plotted results are retained. Substantial new results include NUTS scores across seven models, such as earnings log score -298.03, and earnings training times of 1.96, 4.11, 10.40 and 57.08 minutes for VI, PVI-Log, PVI-CRPS and PVI-IS respectively. Figures 10–12 add convergence, posterior-shape and scaling findings.

T1.justification: Besides the quadratic and CRPS formula corrections, Appendix A.2 corrects differentiation with respect to theta to differentiation with respect to phi. The convergence results and substantive assumptions remain. Uniqueness was already required in v3's formal proposition; making it explicit in the main text does not introduce a new assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and four primary contributions are retained. Section 1.2 adds an explicit scalability claim: parametric variational families support normalizing-flow inference for moderate-dimensional regression and simpler mean-field inference at higher dimensions.

C2.justification: v4 attributes equal election-state variances to model restrictions and adds interpretations concerning computational complexity, regularizer choices and scoring-rule tradeoffs. Section 5 retains slower posterior contraction but removes v3's explicit warning that finite-sample variance cannot distinguish slow convergence from heterogeneity.

D1.justification: v4 newly supplies a code repository link in Section 4, selected regularization settings for each benchmark and variational family in Table 3, NumPyro default-setting information for NUTS, and earnings training times. The selected regularizers disclose outcomes of tuning already described in v3.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds Shen et al. (2025) and Gretton et al. (2012), and expands the discussion of the already-cited McLatchie et al. (2025). It positions PVI's parametric variational implementations relative to these related predictive-inference approaches and their gradient-flow implementations.

P1.justification: v4 makes widespread local copyedits, expands related work, revises the closing discussion and moves the uniqueness explanation from Appendix A.1 into Section 2.4. It adds B.6–B.7 and acknowledgment/impact sections while retaining the overall narrative and section hierarchy.

P2.justification: The main text becomes a two-column conference paper with extensively resized and repositioned displays. Table 2 places diagonal and dense covariance results side by side; Algorithms 1–2, Tables 3–5 and Figures 10–12 are added. v3's Figure 10 and Table 3 are retained as v4's Figure 13 and Table 6.

improvement.justification: Formula corrections improve mathematical consistency, while NUTS comparisons, selected settings, timing and the code link improve assessability and reproducibility. These provide a limited net gain. Material drawbacks remain: Section 5 removes a useful finite-sample heterogeneity warning, and B.7/Figure 12 specifies a likelihood independent of theta, weakening the new scalability demonstration.
